channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Asian equities rally; KOSPI leads gains as US Treasury support counters Fed/Iran risks
item.description: Asian equities advanced on Thursday, with South Korea's KOSPI surging nearly 6% intraday amid a more than 5% jump in SK Hynix shares following the buyback announcement.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD refreshes two-month high as US doubles bond buyback plan
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) posts a fresh two-month high at $67.33 in the Asian trading session on Thursday.

item.title: Gold retreats from June highs as hawkish FOMC minutes and US-Iran tensions support USD
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) eases from its highest level since early June, touched during the Asian session this Thursday, eroding a part of the previous day's strong gains of over 3%.

item.title: Japanese Yen struggles amid widening Trade Deficit, escalating import costs
item.description: USD/JPY appreciates after registering modest losses in the previous day, trading around 158.50 during the Asian hours on Thursday.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar gathers strength to near 0.5950 after China holds loan rates steady in August
item.description: The NZD/USD pair gains momentum to near 0.5950 during the Asian trading hours on Thursday. The pair holds near a two-and-a-half-month high, bolstered by hawkish Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) tone and softer US inflation data.

item.title: China's Commerce Ministry sets anti-dumping tax rates on polyoxymethylene from US, EU, Taiwan and Japan
item.description: China's Commerce Ministry on Thursday announced a decision on corporate tax rate for enterprises related to anti-dumping measures on imported polyoxymethylene from the United States (US), the European Union (EU), Taiwan and Japan, Reuters reported.

item.title: Australia’s Unemployment Rate jumps to 4.5% in July, vs 4.4% expected
item.description: Australia’s Unemployment Rate climbed to 4.5% in July from 4.4% in June, according to the official data released by the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) on Thursday. The figure came in above the market consensus of 4.4%.

item.title: Australian Dollar declines following weak labor data
item.description: AUD/USD depreciates after registering over 0.5% gains in the previous day, trading around 0.7120 during the Asian hours on Thursday. The AUD/USD pair faces downward pressure as the Australian Dollar (AUD) slips in response to a weak domestic labor market report.

item.title: Australian Dollar reacts little to dismal jobs data; holds above weekly low vs weaker JPY
item.description: The AUD/JPY cross attracts some sellers following the release of a dismal Australian jobs report, though it lacks follow-through and holds above the weekly low touched the previous day.

item.title: British Pound edges lower as USD steadies above three-month low; downside seems limited
item.description: The GBP/USD pair edges lower during the Asian session on Thursday and retreats further from its highest level since May 11, touched the previous day.

item.title: WTI surges above $84.50 as Strait of Hormuz standoff escalate
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) oil price appreciates after registering modest losses in the previous day, trading around $85.50 per barrel during the Asian hours on Thursday.

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.7808 vs. 6.7854 previous
item.description: The People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead on Thursday at 6.7808 compared to the previous day's fix of 6.7854 and 6.7196 Reuters estimate.

item.title: PBOC leaves Loan Prime Rates unchanged in August
item.description: The People’s Bank of China (PBOC), China's central bank, announced to leave its Loan Prime Rates (LPRs) unchanged on Thursday. The one-year and five-year LPRs were at 3.00% and 3.50%, respectively.

item.title: Euro edges lower below 1.1700 despite fading Fed hike odds
item.description: The EUR/USD pair posts modest losses around 1.1675 during the early Asian session on Thursday. The Euro (EUR) edges lower against the US Dollar (USD) after experiencing a sharp surge in the previous session.

item.title: US Treasury Department to buy back more longer-term bonds
item.description: The US Treasury Department said on Wednesday that it will buy back more of its longer-term bonds, in an effort to curb a sharp increase in borrowing costs, the Wall Street Journal reported.

item.title: US President Donald Trump announces "crushing economic operation" on Iran
item.description: US President Trump announced the most severe economic action ever taken against Iran, CBS News reported on Wednesday. Trump said this will be economic conflict and isolation on an unprecedented scale and the countries allowing financial aid to Iran will face severe economic consequences.

item.title: Gold climbs above $4,500 as US Dollar, yields fall
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) rises to around $4,520 during the early Asian session on Thursday. The precious metal surges to the highest since early June amid the weakening US Dollar (USD) after the US Treasury Department stepped in to provide relief to bond markets.

item.title: Australian Dollar gains as Treasury buyback offsets hawkish Fed
item.description: The Aussie Dollar advances on Wednesday, up over 0.56%, as the US Dollar registers losses amid the US Treasury bond buyback and despite the release of hawkish Federal Reserve minutes from the July meeting. The AUD/USD trades at 0.7127.

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecast: sellers take control below 50-day SMA
item.description: The GBP/JPY retreats on Wednesday as the cross-pair fails to climb past 216.00 and fell beneath the 50-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) of 125.56. The cross-pair trades at 214.25 down 0.37%.

item.title: Washington bought the Japanese Yen again without meaning to
item.description: USD/JPY closed Wednesday 0.92% lower just above 158.00, the largest single-session decline since the early-August intervention, and Tokyo did not lift a finger for it.

item.title: Pound Sterling's best level since May was made in Washington
item.description: GBP/USD closed Wednesday 0.53% higher just above 1.3600, its best close in three months, and the United Kingdom inflation report that opened the session had almost nothing to do with it. Sterling spent the London morning up barely twenty pips on the day.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar rallies as Treasury buyback drags US yields
item.description: The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) rallies against the US Dollar (USD), pushing north of the 0.5930 mark. The move is driven by broad weakness in the Greenback rather than anything out of New Zealand.

item.title: The Dollar Index answers to the Treasury, not the Fed
item.description: The Dollar Index closed Wednesday 0.86% lower just beneath 98.80, its weakest close since mid-May, and it closed on the session low. The document that did the damage was not a central bank document.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD eyes $67 as US yields slide
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) price reversed course on Wednesday and soared over 5% as US Treasury yields edged lower, following the US Treasury stepping in to cap long-end US bond yields, which had reached levels last seen in 2007.

item.title: Euro surges as traders ignore Fed’s hawkish minutes
item.description: The Euro (EUR) gains over 0.85% against the US Dollar (USD) during the North American session on Wednesday, even though the latest Federal Reserve (Fed) minutes had a hawkish tone, with some participants, along with the three dissenters, suggesting that raising rates could be necessary if the disinf

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar sinks on Treasury buyback ahead of data-heavy Thursday
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) sold off broadly on Wednesday, sinking below the 99.00s region and holding well under 100.00.

item.title: Silver surges as Treasury buyback plan sinks the US Dollar
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) trades sharply higher on Wednesday, changing hands near $65.80. The metal is riding a broad rally across precious metals with Gold (XAU/USD) soaring toward $4,500.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: Franc tests 100-day SMA as US Dollar tanks
item.description: The USD/CHF pair tumbles nearly 2% on Wednesday as a US Treasury buyback announcement sends the Greenback into a tailspin, while US Treasury yields also dive. The pair trades at 0.7979 after reaching a high of 0.8128.

item.title: Gold rallies as buyback sinks yields despite Fed hawkish minutes
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) rallies during Wednesday’s session after the US Federal Reserve (Fed) released the minutes of its July meeting, in which the US central bank held rates unchanged but not unanimously, with three members dissenting and calling for a rate hike.

item.title: Breaking: FOMC officials acknowledged inflation remained elevated
item.description: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) published the Minutes of the July meeting on Wednesday. "The information available at the time of the meeting indicated that inflation remained elevated.
